extracted.intended_audience: newspaper reporters and journalists covering meetings, legislative hearings, investigations, and public bodies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing news stories about meetings, legislative sessions, committees, conventions, and investigatory hearings, with emphasis on accuracy, significance, treatment, and selection of material. Focuses on how to shape often-dry official proceedings into readable, responsible news copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — what counts as a 'meeting' story
rubrics_metrics.description: In the term 'meeting' are included sessions of state legislatures, meetings of municipal councils, conventions of various organizations, meetings of local societies. Investigations and hearings as conducted by committees of legislative bodies are also placed in this class, although they are often more like judicial proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should treat legislative hearings and committee investigations as part of this class and recognize that some of these proceedings resemble court trials in form and handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred form — the purely informative type
rubrics_metrics.description: The purely informative type of story is the common form for reporting meetings, investigations, and hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the parts of the proceedings that are of general interest and significance; these elements should make up the contents of such stories (see cross-references to specific examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and completeness of facts
rubrics_metrics.description: To give the facts accurately and as completely as their significance warrants should be the first aim in reporting proceedings of official bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not distort or suppress facts to accomplish any end, however laudable. A constructive purpose (e.g., exposing sinister influences) is justifiable, but distortion or suppression of facts to make a stronger case is not legitimate. Politically partisan misrepresentation of public matters is improper and damages newspaper credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show significance to readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Much more effort should be made by newspapers ... to show the significance of acts of representative public bodies, in relation not only to the home and business interests of the individual reader, but to the welfare of the community, the state, and the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why actions of governmental and representative bodies matter to readers; use the news columns to create intelligent interest in government and civic affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment — make dry proceedings interesting
rubrics_metrics.description: To make interesting what is often considered dry and unattractive in proceedings of various public meetings is the chief problem in writing news stories concerning them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simple, clear explanation of the meaning of significant parts of the proceedings; provide lively accounts of debate on measures; include vivid description of persons and scenes connected with the meeting. Legitimately bring out humorous or pathetic phases to heighten interest and emphasize significance. Some meetings with slight news interest may be treated humorously as human-interest pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overemphasizing trivial incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Too often, however, insignificant incidents of casual interest are played up as features of meetings of importance to the subordination or even to the exclusion of matters of vital concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist the temptation to spotlight trivial or colorful details at the expense of vital matters; prioritize substantive elements of the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling testimony — treat like court stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony in investigations and hearings sometimes has dramatic phases like that in court trials. The questions and the answers in these proceedings are handled like those in court stories, and testimony is dealt with in much the same manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply techniques used in courtroom reporting — reproduce pertinent Q&A, highlight dramatic or pivotal testimony, and structure testimony coverage clearly and accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and condensation of material
rubrics_metrics.description: To select the vital matters, to present them concisely, and to condense routine but necessary details into the smallest possible compass in stories of this class, require effort and skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify what is essential for readers to know, compress routine procedural details, and present the core issues and outcomes succinctly; this demands judgment and writing skill.
